topic: Dual Pipelines Silently Poison Production ML
postText:
Your ML model scores 98% on offline evaluation, but deploys to production and makes dangerously erratic predictions.
Nobody touched the weights, yet the inference engine is hallucinating risk probabilities.

In healthcare IT systems where I design analytical pipelines, this nightmare is almost never model decay—it is Training-Serving Skew.

Here is what happens under the hood:
Data scientists train models on offline warehouses using heavy batch SQL queries and historical window functions. But in production, the backend extracts features on the fly via microservices, parsing incoming streaming telemetry with distinct edge cases, rounding variances, and timezone mismatches.

Even a single second difference in window calculation (e.g., rolling 60-minute mean vitals) shifts feature vectors outside the model's learned distribution. To the neural net, that slight delta is unseen noise.

How we fix it in mission-critical environments:
1. Unified Feature Stores: Define transformations in one portable spec executed identically online and offline.
2. Temporal Joins: Enforce strict point-in-time correctness during training dataset generation to prevent subtle future data leakage.
3. Shadow Drift Probes: Run automated assertion tests comparing live inference feature snapshots with offline analytical values.

Architectural consistency beats algorithmic complexity every single time.

How do you guarantee strict feature parity between batch training and low-latency real-time inference in your production systems?
